name: Z.ai
summary: Z.ai, also known as Zhipu AI, is an AI company in Beijing. It was [founded in 2019](https://www.qimingvc.com/en/news/china%E2%80%99s-agi-pioneer-and-leader-zai-listed-onhong-kong-stock-exchange) as a Tsinghua University spin-off and makes the GLM models.

incidents.title: Z.ai Did Not Publish Its Promised Seoul Safety Framework
incidents.summary: Zhipu signed the Seoul Frontier AI Safety Commitments in May 2024, which include publishing a severe-risk safety framework before the February 2025 Paris summit. The [Future of Life Institute](https://futureoflife.org/ai-safety-index-summer-2025/) and [SaferAI](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.01166v4) later reported that Zhipu had not published one.
incidents.description: Zhipu (now Z.ai) signed the Seoul Frontier AI Safety Commitments. Under these, it agreed to publish a framework for severe risks by the February 2025 Paris summit. The [Future of Life Institute](https://futureoflife.org/ai-safety-index-summer-2025/) and [SaferAI](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.01166v4) later said that the company had not published one. No company-specific framework has been reported.

timeline.title: Zhipu signs the Seoul commitments
timeline.description: Zhipu.ai is [among 16 companies](https://www.gov.uk/government/news/historic-first-as-companies-spanning-north-america-asia-europe-and-middle-east-agree-safety-commitments-on-development-of-ai) that agree to publish safety frameworks.

timeline.title: Paris summit deadline passes
timeline.description: The [commitments](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/frontier-ai-safety-commitments-ai-seoul-summit-2024/frontier-ai-safety-commitments-ai-seoul-summit-2024) set the AI Summit in France as the publication target.

timeline.title: FLI index notes no framework
timeline.description: The [Summer 2025 AI Safety Index](https://futureoflife.org/ai-safety-index-summer-2025/) says Zhipu AI has not published a framework.

timeline.title: SaferAI lists Zhipu among non-publishers
timeline.description: A [SaferAI study](https://arxiv.org/html/2512.01166v4) of frontier safety frameworks names Zhipu AI among six signatories without a published framework.

timeline.title: FLI index again notes no framework
timeline.description: The [Summer 2026 AI Safety Index](https://futureoflife.org/ai-safety-index-summer-2026/) says Z.ai has no published framework.

timeline.title: Z.ai co-writes an open-weight risk framework
timeline.description: Concordia AI and Z.AI [announce](https://concordia-ai.com/research/frontier-open-weight-ai-risk-management-framework/) a general framework for open-weight developers.

sources.title: Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Seoul Summit 2024
Historic first as companies spanning North America, Asia, Europe and Middle East agree safety commitments on development of AI
Evaluating AI Providers' Frontier AI Safety Frameworks

incidents.title: Evaluators Report Weak Misuse Safeguards in Z.ai's Open-Weight GLM-5 Models
incidents.summary: External evaluators reported that Z.ai's open-weight GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 models have strong offensive-cyber capabilities and safeguards that are easy to bypass or remove. [Anthropic said](https://www.anthropic.com/research/glm-5-3-and-the-spread-of-advanced-cyber-capabilities) attackers could bypass GLM-5.3's safeguards between 64% and 100% of the time in its simulated tests.
incidents.description: External evaluators reported that Z.ai's open-weight GLM-5.2 and GLM-5.3 models have strong cyber-attack capabilities and weak safeguards. [SaferAI said](https://www.safer-ai.org/research/glm-5-2-evaluation-report) that GLM-5.2 refused none of its offensive-security or biological tasks. Z.ai delayed the GLM-5.3 weight release for a safety review, but [Anthropic said](https://www.anthropic.com/research/glm-5-3-and-the-spread-of-advanced-cyber-capabilities) that attackers could bypass its safeguards in 64% to 100% of simulated tests.

timeline.title: SaferAI publishes GLM-5.2 evaluation
timeline.description: SaferAI [reports](https://www.safer-ai.org/research/glm-5-2-evaluation-report) that GLM-5.2 refused none of its offensive-security or biological tasks.

timeline.title: Z.ai announces GLM-5.3 with delayed weight release
timeline.description: Z.ai [says](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/china-ai-new-model-glm-anthropic-mythos-5-6319716) it will release weights after a two-week safety review and limit sensitive cyber functions to verified users.

timeline.title: GLM-5.3 weights released
timeline.description: Z.ai [publicly releases the weights](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/09/caisis-assessment-zais-glm-53-cyber-capabilities) two weeks after launch.

timeline.title: CAISI publishes its assessment
timeline.description: NIST's CAISI [calls](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2026/09/caisis-assessment-zais-glm-53-cyber-capabilities) GLM-5.3 the most cyber-capable open-weight model to date.

timeline.title: Anthropic reports safeguards are easy to bypass
timeline.description: Anthropic [reports](https://www.anthropic.com/research/glm-5-3-and-the-spread-of-advanced-cyber-capabilities) bypass rates of 64% to 100% in simulated tests.

timeline.title: Irregular reports no refusals on offensive tasks
timeline.description: Irregular [reports](https://www.irregular.com/research/glm-5.3-multi-stage-cyber-operations-and-instruction-violations) that GLM-5.3 refused none of the offensive tasks it tested and completed 3 of 13 multi-stage attack scenarios.

timeline.title: Epoch AI reports Firefox exploits with no refusals
timeline.description: Epoch AI [says](https://epoch.ai/publications/open-weight-models-patch-gap) that GLM-5.3 built working exploits for six Firefox releases at about $1,000 each, and that no provider, including Z.ai, refused or restricted the requests.

incidents.title: Z.ai's ZCode Uploaded Local Code Repositories Without Clear Consent
incidents.summary: A developer found that Z.ai's ZCode coding assistant packaged users' whole workspaces, including Git history, and tried to upload them to Alibaba Cloud storage. Z.ai [apologised, removed the feature and said third parties verified the data was deleted](https://technode.com/2026/09/29/zhipus-zcode-deletes-data-and-announces-compensation-after-data-upload-controversy/).
incidents.description: [A developer found](https://technode.com/2026/09/29/zhipus-zcode-deletes-data-and-announces-compensation-after-data-upload-controversy/) that Z.ai's ZCode coding assistant packaged local workspaces, including source code and Git history, and tried to upload them to Alibaba Cloud storage. The feature was on by default, and users had no clear way to stop it. Z.ai apologised, removed the feature and [said](https://www.infoworld.com/article/4225022/z-ai-disables-coding-assistant-feature-after-flaw-exposed-enterprise-code-upload-risk.html) that it did not keep the data or use it for model training.

timeline.title: Developer finds repository snapshot; Z.ai apologises
timeline.description: A developer [reports](https://technode.com/2026/09/29/zhipus-zcode-deletes-data-and-announces-compensation-after-data-upload-controversy/) a 313 MB workspace archive, and Z.ai apologises.

timeline.title: ZCode 3.14.0 removes the upload path
timeline.description: The [new release](https://technode.com/2026/09/29/zhipus-zcode-deletes-data-and-announces-compensation-after-data-upload-controversy/) removes the Repo Wiki entry and the snapshot upload paths.

timeline.title: Z.ai open-sources ZCode and shares first audit results
timeline.description: Z.ai [says](https://www.infoworld.com/article/4225022/z-ai-disables-coding-assistant-feature-after-flaw-exposed-enterprise-code-upload-risk.html) NSFOCUS confirmed deletion of the bucket and its contents.

timeline.title: Remediation complete; compensation announced
timeline.description: Z.ai [announces](https://technode.com/2026/09/29/zhipus-zcode-deletes-data-and-announces-compensation-after-data-upload-controversy/) completed remediation and compensation for all users.

sources.title: Zhipu's ZCode deletes data and announces compensation after data upload controversy
Z.ai disables coding assistant feature after flaw exposed enterprise code upload risk

incidents.title: Unit 42 Says Suspected China-Nexus Attackers Used Z.ai's GLM-5.2 in Autonomous Intrusions
incidents.summary: [Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 said](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cairn-framework-ai-autonomous-attacks/) that a suspected China-nexus group used the open-source Cairn framework with Z.ai's GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek V4 models to attack at least 19 organizations in August and September 2026. It said the attacks got access or data at 10 organizations, and that neither model refused a simple "authorized testing" pretext.
incidents.description: [Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 said](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cairn-framework-ai-autonomous-attacks/) that a suspected China-nexus group used Z.ai's GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek V4 models with the open-source Cairn framework to attack at least 19 organizations in August 2026. According to Unit 42, the attackers got access or data at 10 of them. The models did not refuse a simple "authorized testing" pretext, the report said.

timeline.title: Unit 42 publishes its report
timeline.description: Unit 42 [describes](https://www.cybersecuritydive.com/news/china-hacker-ai-tool-campaign-us-defense-semiconductor/874619/) attacks on semiconductor, defense and civil-society organizations.

sources.title: Attackers Use Autonomous AI to Target Semiconductor, Defense and Civil Society Sectors
